$description: Tokens the board's JavaScript (or, for the urgency cue, a component rule) writes live; the value here is what everything else reads.

source.reason: the column's own colour, written onto the column element by Column.tsx; this is what a surface outside a coloured column reads.
the same on hover, written by Column.tsx; fully opaque is what every other column reads.
how faded a parked column is, written onto the column element by Column.tsx; fully opaque is what every other column reads.

the folder context's colour, written onto the card by CardItem.tsx. Declared `initial` — the guaranteed-invalid value — because a card can have a context and no colour, and the strip and the chip answer that differently on purpose; a real value here would silently change both.
the height the rendered description is capped at, measured and written by CardDetail.tsx; this is the figure used before it measures.

how much the last card must clear the app's floating status bar, written onto the board root by App.tsx once it has measured the real bar; this is what stands in before it does. A guess at a measurement is not a spacing decision — moving the grid must not move it, and measuring the bar must.
the due-date cue's colour, set per urgency by the rules in cards.css; transparent is the resting value for a card with no urgency.
the faint wash behind the same cue, set per urgency by the rules in cards.css; the `soon` state deliberately leaves it at the resting value.

the guaranteed-invalid value, so the one swatch rule can read a fill the palette row writes inline while the "no colour" swatch, which is the same class with nothing written onto it, falls through to its own background.
